title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 83-85): Grothendieck is computing, in completely explicit generators, the 'Teichmüller-type' fundamental groups attached to a very symmetric map (carte) P on the sphere. The map is the regular n-gon: vertex set S, edge set A, and faces ω. Σ* is the sphere punctured at the vertices, and Π_P = π_1(Σ*, P_ω) is based at the centre P_ω of a face. It is generated by the loops ρ_s (s ∈ S, numbered ρ_0..ρ_{n-1}) and the ε_s, with ρ_s = ε_s^2.

The groups involved:
- D_P is the group of orientation-preserving automorphisms of the map. It is dihedral of order 2n, generated by the rotation ρ (order n about P_ω) and the half-turn σ_a about the midpoint Q_a of an edge a. The half-turn σ_{a0} swaps the two faces and the vertices 0 and 1.
- Π_P^D is the extension of D_P by Π_P, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of Σ*/D_P.
- τ_a are orientation-reversing reflections (complex conjugations).
- Π_P^{D,τ} is the extended group including the anti-holomorphic symmetries.
- The lifts g ↦ g̃ (g ∈ D_P) act on Π_P by transport of structure, with sign sg(g) = ±1 according to whether g preserves orientation.

This page:
(82) Specialising to g = σ_a°: σ̃_a(ε_s) = ε_{σ_a°(s)}^{-1} and σ̃_a(ρ_s) = ρ_{σ_a°(s)}^{-1}. Writing σ_{a0} = σ̃_{a0} τ_{a0} then gives the action of σ_{a0} on Π_P: it swaps ρ_0 and ρ_1, and sends ρ_i to a conjugate of ρ_{n+1-i}, where the conjugator is a product of consecutive ρ's (2 ≤ i ≤ n-1). This is the braid-like action of the mapping class on the standard generators of the free group of the punctured sphere.

A marginal NB describes the action of τ_a as a composite: the map induced by σ_a° from π_1(Σ*, P_ω) to π_1(Σ*, P_ω'), followed by the change-of-basepoint isomorphism λ_a back to P_ω.

(84) Π_P^{D,τ} ≅ Π_P^D ⋊ {1, τ_{a0}}.

(85) Explicit action: τ_{a0}(ρ) = σ_{a0} ρ^{-1} σ_{a0} and τ_{a0}(σ_{a0}) = σ_{a0}. The first relation comes from τ_{a0}(ρ τ_{a0} ρ^{-1}) = τ_{a0} τ_{a1} = ρ_1^{-1} = (ρ σ ρ σ)^{-1} = σ ρ^{-1} σ ρ^{-1}.

Rewriting with the orientation-reversing lift σ̃_{a0} = σ_{a0} τ_{a0}^{-1} gives the 'prettier' form (86):
- Π_P^{D,τ} ≅ Π_P^D ⋊ {1, σ̃_{a0}}, with σ̃(ρ) = ρ^{-1} and σ̃(σ) = σ.
- Presentation: ⟨ρ, σ, σ̃ | ρ^n = σ^2 = σ̃^2 = (σσ̃)^2 = (σ̃ρ)^2 = 1⟩.

Geometrically, σ̃_{a0} is a reflection fixing the base point P_ω, so it inverts the rotation ρ; Grothendieck calls this 'trivial'. Since Π_P^D ≅ Z/n * Z/2 (the Hecke group, orbifold π_1 of P^1 with signature ∞, 2, n), Π_P^{D,τ} is the extended Hecke group. Page 85 rewrites it as the amalgam D_n *_{Z/2} (Z/2 × Z/2). For n = 3 this is PSL_2(Z) and PGL_2(Z).

Purpose: an explicit model case (the regular n-gon map) of how the full symmetry group of a map, including orientation-reversing ones, acts on the fundamental group of the punctured surface. This is part of the 1981 'Teichmülleries' programme relating maps and dessins to Teichmüller and modular groups.
errors: Index inconsistency: the marginal formula σ̃_{a0}(ρ_i) = ρ_{n-i}^{-1} (reflection i ↦ -i, fixing vertex 0) does not match σ_{a0} swapping ρ_0 and ρ_1, i.e. i ↦ 1-i ≡ n+1-i, which is used two lines later. Either the margin should read ρ_{1-i}^{-1}, or σ̃_{a0} is a reflection through a different axis. Minor bookkeeping only.

The conjugating words in the σ_{a0}(ρ_i) and τ_{a0}(ρ_i) formulas are written loosely ('commence avec ρ_i, finis ρ_{i+1}' on the previous page), and Grothendieck himself flags a τ_{a0} vs τ_0 mix-up. The final group-level statements (84)-(86) are nevertheless correct.

ideas.what: Action of the lifted map automorphisms (holomorphic and antiholomorphic) on the free generators ρ_s, ε_s of π_1 of the punctured sphere, with sign sg(g)
ideas.modern_name: Action of the (extended) automorphism group of a regular map / dessin on the fundamental group; outer action of the extended mapping class group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hurwitz, Dyck); in dessin form Jones–Singerman 1978, Grothendieck 1984
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this explicit computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Π_P^D ≅ Z/n * Z/2 and Π_P^{D,τ} ≅ (Z/n * Z/2) ⋊ Z/2, with σ̃ inverting ρ and fixing σ; presentation with ρ^n = σ^2 = σ̃^2 = (σσ̃)^2 = (σ̃ρ)^2 = 1
ideas.modern_name: Hecke group and extended Hecke group; PSL_2(Z) and PGL_2(Z) for n = 3; extended triangle group (2, n, ∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hecke (1936); extended Hecke groups classical (Coxeter); PGL_2(Z) ≅ D_2 *_{Z/2} D_3 classical

ideas.what: Using the orientation-reversing lift σ̃ (based at the face centre) instead of τ to get the simplest semidirect-product presentation
ideas.modern_name: Choice of reflection generators for an extended triangle/Coxeter-type group

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard computation: the extended Hecke group presentation and its amalgam decomposition are classical. Its interest is purely historical, showing Grothendieck in 1981 treating real (antiholomorphic) structures on maps and computing explicit actions on π_1 generators. Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In the derivation of (85), '= ρ^{-1} = (ρσ_{a0}ρσ_{a0})^{-1}' should read '= ρ_1^{-1} = (ρσ_{a0}ρσ_{a0})^{-1}'. It is the vertex loop ρ_1 (cf. ρ_1 = ρσ_{a0}ρσ_{a0} on the previous page), not the rotation ρ.
'(84) Π_{P_τ}^{D,τ}' is Π_P^{D,τ} with a stray subscript; the equation number in the image may read (83)/(84).

The garbled 'puisque ρ = ω̃ ... A' is roughly 'puisque ρ = ω̃ ...' followed by a statement that g ↦ g̃ is a group homomorphism D_P → Π_P^{D,τ}. The 'Π_1^{P,τ}' in the transcription should be Π_P^{D,τ}.
Margin: 'd'où σ̃_{a0}(ρ_i) = ρ_{n-i}^{-1}' (the index may be 1-i).
